title: Pepper-spray thief hits store
article: A robbery at a southwest Shoppers Drug Mart on Sunday left employees and customers gasping for breath when a pepper-based spray was released in the store.
Around 3:30 p.m., a man entered the store at 1515 8th St. S.W. and went to the pharmacy at the back.
"He released pepper spray or bear spray and demanded drugs," said police Insp. Peter Davison, adding that the culprit fled with an unknown quantity of drugs.
Employees said they saw the man run out of the store with a bag before they realized what was happening.
"All of a sudden, you couldn't breathe," said Ann Paniec, who works in the cosmetic section of the Shoppers Drug Mart in Connaught.
She said everyone in the store was choking and gagging.
Kevin Howell, another employee, said it was difficult to breathe.
"There was an orange haze all over the place," he said.
About a dozen people suffered side-effects such as coughing, burning eyes and throat irritation.
Doug Odney, a spokesman for Calgary Emergency Medical Services, said six people were treated and released at the scene.
"No one was sprayed directly," he said.
Odney said although the spray was released at the back of the building, it filled the store in a relatively short time.
Paniec and Howell, both with watery eyes, said they had to wait for all of the customers to leave the store before they could depart.
And while it wasn't the first time the store has been robbed, the pair agreed it could have been a lot worse.

On Dec. 23, 2000, a Calgary police officer fatally shot 34-year- old Arthur George Provencal in the head as he held a knife to the throat of a pharmacist during a bungled robbery at the Shoppers Drug Mart in TD Square.
"Thank God it was just pepper spray," said Paniec, in reference to the previous incident.
